passages.p1: The Temperate Zone has four seasons: spring, summer, autumn, and winter. Temperature and rainfall are mostly mild. Mild means not too hot and not too cold.
passages.p2: Oceanic Climates have mild summers and mild winters, with mild rainfall all year. Mediterranean Climates are dry in summer, with mild rainfall in winter.
passages.p3: Places near the Tropical Zone have Subtropical Climates. Humid Subtropical Climates have very hot summers and mild winters. Rain falls all year, but a lot falls in summer.
passages.p4: Naha is the capital city of Okinawa. It has a Humid Subtropical Climate. The summer is hot and the winter is mild. There is no dry season.
passages.p5: Places near the Polar Zone have Subpolar Climates. Subpolar Climates have mild summers and very cold winters. Irkutsk is a city in Siberia with a Subpolar Climate.
passages.p6: Irkutsk does not have much rain or snow in winter. Most rain falls in summer. The rainiest month is July, when the weather is warmest.
passages.p7: In winter, temperatures go below minus 10 degrees. People wear fur coats and fur hats. They go skiing and play ice hockey.
passages.p8: Thick ice covers rivers and lakes, and trucks can drive on them. Once, the temperature was minus 67.7 degrees in Oymyakon Village. Summer temperatures sometimes go close to 30 degrees.
passages.p9: Subpolar Climates have forests because of the warm summers. Coniferous trees, such as fir and pine, have cones. The coniferous forests in Siberia are called Taiga.
passages.p10: Under the Taiga, there is soil called permafrost that is always frozen. When the permafrost melts, land sinks. People build houses on stilts so that the permafrost won’t melt.
passages.p11: Many people in Siberia work in forestry and mining. But with global warming, cutting down the forests causes problems. The sun shining on the ground is melting the permafrost.
passages.p12: Dachas are small country houses with vegetable gardens. Many people move to dachas in the summer and grow vegetables. Now life is easier, with fresh vegetables in supermarkets all year.

passages.p1: Many farmers still use old methods to grow potatoes and corn. Agricultural corporations use advanced technology to grow cash crops such as coffee and sugarcane.
passages.p2: Corporations received a lot of money from the government and from countries such as the United States and Japan.
passages.p3: Coffee, soybeans, meat, sugar, and bioethanol are important exports. South America also has a lot of minerals, such as oil, copper, and iron ore.
passages.p4: The governments of South America worked hard to mine minerals. Their economies grew by exporting them.
passages.p5: Japan imports a lot of iron ore and copper from South America. Brazil now makes cars and airplanes.
passages.p6: Many people are worried about environmental problems, such as forest areas decreasing. After 1970, corporations cut down large areas of tropical rainforest in the Amazon Basin.
passages.p7: Traditional farmers cut down trees but protected the forests. Corporations cut down many more trees and destroyed the forests.
passages.p8: Growing the same crops on the same land makes the soil poor. Crops don’t grow well, and agriculture is hard to continue.
passages.p9: Tropical rainforests have many kinds of plants and animals, but many of them are disappearing. Once they are gone, they will never return.
passages.p10: Too much mining destroys the environment. When the minerals are gone, the mining industry will also disappear.
